articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft patches 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. When AI finds bugs faster than humans can patch them, you know we're living in interesting times.

articles.title: Internal Pentagon Report Reveals Hegseth Is Willfully Putting Civilians in Danger
articles.summary: Second CVSS 10.0 Cisco SD-WAN zero-day this year gets actively exploited because apparently network administrators love maximum severity Tuesdays. Some vulnerabilities are so perfect they make you weep.

articles.title: Frequently asked questions about the continued exploitation of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-20182)
articles.summary: Microsoft Exchange Server gets pwned via crafted email because irony isn't dead yet. CVE-2026-42897 proves that sometimes the oldest attack vectors are still the best attack vectors.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas platform gets ransomed, disrupting education nationwide because apparently criminals have decided that homework is the real enemy. Nothing says 'digital chaos' like defacing a login page with extortion demands.

articles.title: On-Prem Microsoft Exchange Server CVE-2026-42897 Exploited via Crafted Email
articles.summary: OpenAI gets bit by TanStack supply chain attack hitting two employee devices, proving even the AI overlords can't escape npm's cursed dependency hell. At least they caught it before Skynet got embarrassing.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN  to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: Foxconn cyberattack allegedly steals files from Apple, Intel, Google, Dell, and NVIDIA because why hack one tech giant when you can collect them all? Supply chain attacks are the new Pokemon cards.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram kills its barely-used end-to-end encryption feature because technical challenges are hard and user privacy is apparently optional. Another day, another broken promise from Big Tech.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Victory dance time: Apple finally enables end-to-end encryption for RCS between Android and iPhone. Only took them forever to stop making our messages NSA-readable by default.

articles.title: The Boring Stuff is Dangerous Now
articles.summary: EFF launches campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid, a blogger and open-source advocate who started contributing to Wikipedia at age 12. Because defending digital freedom fighters never goes out of style.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider member 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after SMS phishing attacks. Another cybercrime legend trades lulz for orange jumpsuits and federal time.
